articleTitle: Design of PID-Based Buck-Boost Converter for Battery Charging in Regenerative Braking System of BLDC Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: As human life evolves, energy consumption increases significantly, prompting various efforts to conserve energy. One such effort involves transitioning from gasoline vehicles to electric ones, focusing on energy savings based on LCGC and zero emissions. This led to research on regenerative braking systems using a Buck-Boost Converter with PID control. The study conducted two sets of tests: one with PID control and another without. Determination of PID parameter value in this research using trial and error method. The motor used was a BLDC motor with a 12 V/12 Ah battery, where the charging voltage limit was 14.7 Volts. Researchers conducted test with varying duty Cyle values, namely duty-cyle values 30% to 60%. From the results of testing without control, the highest battery charging efficiency value is obtained when braking, which is 90.1% with a duty-cyle value of 40%. While the test results using PID control, obtained the highest battery charging efficiency value of 90,63%, with Kp=2, Ki=0,4 and Kd=20.

articleTitle: Vehicle Speed Estimation System and Automatic License Plate Recognition using Yolov8 and EasyOCR on Traffic Camera Footage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: The latest vehicle detection technology has enabled the development of systems that can detect vehicles, estimate speed, and automatically recognize vehicle license plates. In this study, a program was created that uses two different YOLO (You Only Look Once) models for vehicle and license plate detection in the video. The YOLOv8 model is used to detect vehicles, while the special model is used to detect license plates. In the EasyOCR program is a library used for reading vehicle license plates. The program can also detect whether the driver is violating the traffic speed limit. The results of the experiment showed an accuracy level of 91.87% for vehicle speed estimation and 96.87% for automatic license plate recognition. This can be influenced by several factors that can affect the accuracy of vehicle speed estimates and automatic license plate readings. One of these factors that most affects the results is the angle of the shooting.

articleTitle: UGER: Enhancing the Quality of ROUV Image Segmentation with CLAHE and Color Space-Morphology Masking Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: This research aims to enhance the quality of image segmentation captured by Remotely Operated Underwater Vehicles (ROUVs) using contrast-limited adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) and color space masking morphology techniques. We employ three primary metrics, namely Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), Structural Similarity Index (SSIM), and Video Multi-method Assessment Fusion (VMAF), to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed methods. The analysis results demonstrate that applying CLAHE and color space-morphology masking significantly improves image segmentation quality. Data obtained from various environments, such as swimming pools, rivers, and fish ponds, show consistent improvements in image reconstruction, structural similarity, and overall video quality. This study makes a significant contribution to underwater image processing, enhancing the applications of underwater monitoring and exploration with more accurate and high-quality image segmentation.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of BLDC Motor Drive with Bipolar PWM Six-Step Commutation for Speed Regulation System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: This paper presents the speed regulation of the brushless direct current (BLDC) motor. The parameters of the BLDC motor were discovered and evaluated by experimental work. Speed regulation for BLDC motor drive is crucial, used to get a quick response when the speed changes. The speed control used the concept of bipolar pulsed width modulation (PWM) six-step commutation. The control method used is Proportional-Integrator (PI) with parameter Kp = 0.008 and Ki = 0.1. The speed of the BLDC motor can be controlled using PI control based on the appropriate reference value. At nominal speed and torque, the system without PI control generates error steady state (ESS) by 0.0124% with a settling time of 0.12 s and the oscillation undergoes in the system. In a closed-loop system with PI control, ESS generated is 0.0032% with a settling time of 0.014 s. The designed PI control can significantly reduce ESS by 74% on a system compared to ESS without PI control, so the system works in steady condition.

articleTitle: Fuzzy-Logic Based Fast-Charger Design For Lithium Polymer Battery Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Electrical energy usage is significant in Indonesia, driven by the growing dependence on electronic devices, with batteries used for energy storage in appliances. Continuous battery use reduces capacity, prompting electronics manufacturers to enhance battery capacity with lithium batteries. The battery recharging process is defined by optimal time and efficiency for immediate device use. However, long charging times and high temperatures during charging can damage the battery. This research aims to create a method for fast-charging Lithium Polymer batteries. A fuzzy logic control system will be employed to regulate the voltage and current, as well as to maintain the battery temperature within an optimal range. The regulation of the charger voltage is achieved through an increase from the PWM-generated output voltage of 12.6 Volts to a maximum of 13.5 Volts, thereby facilitating a more expeditious charging of the Lithium Polymer battery. The optimal time for fast battery charging with fuzzy logic control is 55 minutes, with the first temperature of 28.38°C and the second temperature of 28.44°C. Meanwhile, without control, the optimal charging time is 45 minutes, with the first temperature of 37.69°C and the second temperature of 37.60°C. Nevertheless, a fuzzy control system for battery charging is designed to reduce the temperature of the battery to a level that will not overload it and extend its lifespan.

articleTitle: Voice Signal-Based Wheelchair Navigation Control Using Convolutional Neural Network for Cerebral Palsy Patients
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: This research applies the use of a convolutional neural network (CNN) in speech recognition to control a wheelchair, with a focus on cerebral palsy patients. In the context of the mobility and independence of such patients, speech recognition becomes an alternative solution to traditional joysticks that may be difficult to use by patients with hand impairments. In an effort to improve accessibility and quality of life for patients, this research proposes the use of CNN technology to efficiently detect voice commands. Through the evaluation of the CNN model using two different testing stages. The results show significant accuracy levels, with offline testing achieving optimal accuracy of up to 100% on validation data. Although testing with test data revealed a decrease in accuracy to approximately 95.70%, real-time testing showed an average accuracy of 74%.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of LoRa Network Application in Power Transformer Monitoring with IoT Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Transformers are vital components in the electrical network, with the main function of changing the electrical voltage according to operational needs. Along with the development of technology, traditional monitoring methods using analog meters and manual readings are starting to be replaced by more sophisticated digital systems, such as the Internet of Things (IoT). Previous studies have developed various transformer monitoring methods by utilizing IoT, algorithms, and other approaches to improve accuracy and efficiency. However, further development is still needed to improve the efficiency of energy management in transformers. This study proposes the development of an IoT-based transformer monitoring system that uses LoRa (Long-Range) communication to transmit monitoring data. As a result, the LoRa Ebyte E32 DTU Module is able to transmit data in indoor and outdoor conditions with varying ranges. However, this test was only carried out at a height of 1 meter from the ground where in sending data, the height between points needs to be higher than 1 meter. Trial delivery with distance between units gradually from 150 meters to 2.5 kilometers.

articleTitle: Design of Circular Microstrip Antenna for Partial Discharge Measurement in High Voltage Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: In this study a circular microstrip antenna was designed to detect partial discharge (PD) in high voltage equipment. This antenna design has a relatively small size. It could detect PD in air, oil and solid insulation media. There are several ways to achieve the expected results as designed an antenna, including cutting the ground and adding an 'i' slot to the antenna ground by trial and error to achieve the objective of antenna. The advantage of this antenna is that it can detect in a horizontal or vertical position. The goals used in the parameters of this antenna include operating frequencies of 200 MHz - 1.8 GHz, return loss less than -10 dB, VSWR (Voltage Standing Wave Ratio) less than 2, input impedance of 50 Ω, gain value greater than 2 dB and omnidirectional radiation pattern. The result antenna design uses an 18 x 11 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> circular patch and is proven to detect partial discharge in air, oil and solid insulation media. According to the simulation results, this antenna design has an optimum frequency of 0.94 GHz.

articleTitle: Simulation of a Coffee Bean Drying System Using Solar Panels and Microwave
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: In this era of increasingly advanced technology, the coffee bean drying system still relies heavily on conventional drying systems. Either using direct solar energy or a mechanical drying system with fuel as a main supply of energy. This paper presents to observe and analyze from electrical energy side based on method that drying coffee beans as dielectric material using solar panels or photovoltaic and microwave. The output power of the PV result is based on the time that PV gets irradiance, from 7.00 AM to 17.00 PM. Other than that hour, the output power of PV is zero because the value of irradiance is zero. At 7.00 AM the output power of PV is 175,898 W. At 12.00 PM, the output power of PV is 4099,2 W. At 17.00 PM, the output power is 27,7344 W. The power value of the boost converter at 7.00 AM is 50,1018 W. The highest power value is 1192,63 W at 12.00 PM. The lowest power value is 7,376 W at 17.00 PM. The lowest power of the inverter is 23,303 W at 17.00 PM. The highest power is 3612,109 W at 12.00 PM. The initial humidity value is 60%, the initial mass 667,5 kg, and assume that the mass at a time is 557,5 kg, the value of humidity at a time is 71,64% and the result of final moisture or water content is 2,526%.

articleTitle: D-STATCOM Four-Leg Intelligent Control System for Unbalance and Non Linear Load Harmonic Compensator using Fuzzy based on IRPT Control Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Reactive power compensation traditionally relies on devices like Static VAR Compensators (SVCs) and reactor/capacitor banks. While effective, these systems have significant drawbacks, including large size, high losses, restricted bandwidth, and slow response times. To address these issues, inverter-based power quality conditioners, such as D-STATCOMs, have emerged as modern solutions. D-STATCOMs offer rapid response, compact design, and lower losses, effectively regulating reactive power through a dc bus capacitor, solid-state devices, and ac inductors. Control methodologies typically utilize Fuzzy controllers enhances this control strategy. These controllers take error values of e and e as input and their variations voltage as a input parameters. They also mitigate system unbalances and nonlinear loads, effectively reducing harmonics and the ripples. One of the significant advantages of Fuzzy controllers is their reduced reliance on complex mathematical models, simplifying the design process. This makes them more accessible and practical for implementation. To decide the parameters, this paper using e and ∆e Reff for the input values. Rule base and parameter attached, and Fuzzy can reduce the harmonic and the ripple.

articleTitle: Hybrid Method for Photovoltaic System Forecasting Based on Wavelet Transform and LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) forecasting is done to help in managing planning and knowing PV energy production. However, PV systems are always associated with fluctuating weather parameters, such as solar irradiance, temperature, wind speed, and humidity. In order, to forecast uncertain data, this object over here study proposed a combination method by using a concept of wavelet transform (WT) and the ability of long-short-term memory (LSTM). The WT is used to decompose the output power with the feature extraction process. Then it is used as input to the LSTM to forecast the futuristic value of output power. The forecasting results are shown in a curve and compared with actual data at several time horizons of 1 day, 15 days, 30 days, and 60 days. In addition, the results are also compared with several other ML methods such as Ridge Regression (RR), Linear Regression (LR), Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO), and Elastic Net (ENET). Each of these treatments shows that the forecasting results using the proposed method are superior. This is also supported by evidence on the percent error values of Root mean squared error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), and coefficient of determination (R2)

articleTitle: Temperature Control in Coffee Bean Dryer Using Fuzzy Logic Control with Multiple Input and Multiple Output
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Digital transformation brings many conveniences to society, especially in the field of agricultural technology. One implementation of the use of digital transformation in agricultural technology is the creation of an automatic coffee bean dryer. This study aims to improve the quality of coffee bean drying by using a coffee bean dryer that is regulated using a temperature control system based on Fuzzy Logic Control (FLC). The main focus of this study is temperature regulation with a setpoint of 60 ℃ to achieve a coffee bean moisture content of less than 12.5%, according to international export standards. The control system used is Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) using FLC, which provides valve values and rotary dryer speeds based on the actual temperature read. With this control, two inputs are needed, namely temperature error and temperature delta error, and will produce two outputs in the form of gas stove valve settings and blower speed. The study results show that this coffee bean dryer system can maintain a stable temperature with a very small error. The highest temperature above the setpoint is only 0.45 ℃ (0.75%), and the lowest temperature below the setpoint is only 0.2 ℃ (0.33%). The addition of blower settings has proven effective in maintaining temperature stability during the drying process, so it is expected to improve the quality of the coffee beans produced.

articleTitle: Mobile-Based Nutrition and Physical Activity Management for Diabetes Patients Using Google Fit and React Native
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: In modern society, unhealthy diets are a significant contributor to the prevalence of diabetes, a chronic condition that disrupts the body's ability to regulate blood glucose levels. Effective diabetes management requires a combination of regular physical activity and medical nutritional therapy. Daily caloric needs, which are critical for managing diabetes, vary based on individual factors such as height, weight, gender, age, and level of physical activity. This study introduces DiaDoc, a Diabetes Health Management System that leverages mobile technology to manage nutrition and physical activity. The system utilizes the "Guidelines for the Management and Prevention of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus in Indonesia 2021" to calculate personalized daily calorie requirements and generate tailored food recommendations for users. Additionally, the Google Fit API is integrated to monitor users' physical activity by tracking their step counts. Five users participated in a feature test involving twelve tasks to evaluate the system, achieving a 94.1% success rate, indicating the application's high functionality and usability. The system's accuracy and effectiveness were further validated by a nutritionist, who used the application’s calculations and nutritional advice to assess its performance, resulting in an overall score of 80%. Furthermore, a three-day validation test with five patients demonstrated a 3.44% improvement in fasting blood sugar (FBS) stability, highlighting the application’s potential in assisting patients with diabetes to manage their blood sugar levels effectively.

articleTitle: Sharding Blockchain Model to Reduce The Costs of Presidential Elections In Indonesia Base on Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Presidential elections in Indonesia are held every five years as part of political and democratic activities to elect Indonesia's future leaders. Currently, the presidential election process is supported by a conventional information system that collects vote count results per region and accumulates them in stages at the national level. The data and information produced by this system are at high risk of being manipulated. Several cases in the 2024 Indonesian presidential election show a lot of fraud by manipulating the vote count results. Several studies propose the use of a system based on blockchain technology to increase transparency and security in collecting vote count results in the presidential election in Indonesia. However, the vast territory of Indonesia, spread over several islands with hundreds of millions of voters, makes blockchain technology inefficient for presidential elections in Indonesia. Thus, the problem statement of this research is how the concept of blockchain sharding can increase the efficiency of applying blockchain technology to presidential elections in Indonesia. The research uses a qualitative approach with a literature review regarding blockchain technology-based systems to support presidential elections in Indonesia and the concept of blockchain sharding. The research output is a blockchain sharding adoption model to increase the efficiency of adopting blockchain technology for the presidential election in Indonesia. The paper also includes simulations with the Hyperledger.

articleTitle: Implementation of YOLO and Face Recognition on a Security Camera System for Visitor Detection in the Computer and Network Lab of UNS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Traditional security camera systems (CCTV cameras) only record video without automatic analysis, necessitating continuous human monitoring. This approach is inefficient and prone to human error. This research aims to implement the "You Only Look Once" (YOLO) method for object detection and face recognition in a security camera system to detect visitors to the computer and network laboratory at Sebelas Maret University (UNS). The study uses quantitative methods to measure the success rate of the system in identifying and tracking visitors entering the laboratory. The visitor counting program is implemented using Python, while the face recognition program utilizes API concepts in JavaScript to receive input from the visitor counting program. The results of the study show that the YOLO and face recognition programs perform well at a distance of 4 meters, outperforming other distance conditions. The programs work effectively under bright lighting conditions; however, under dark conditions, only the visitor counting program functions properly. Under optimal conditions, the object detection system achieves 99% accuracy, and the visitor counting system operates efficiently in both quiet (single person entry/exit) and busy (multiple people entry/exit) scenarios. The face recognition system also achieves 84% accuracy for 50 individuals across 5 classes under optimal conditions.

articleTitle: Smart Parking System with IoT-Enabled using NodeMCU for Car Reservation in Public Areas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: This paper presents the smart parking system using NodeMCU ESP8266 for web-based car reservation in public areas. Conventional parking system made car users take a long time to find the parking in public areas like shopping centers or malls. Therefore, its necessary to overcome this problem by implementing the smart parking system of car reservation. The system prototype integrates the Internet of Things (IoT) technology, NodeMCU ESP8266 (microcontroller), Ultrasonic Sensor HC-SR04 (vehicle detector sensor in parking area), IR obstacle sensor (entry and exit), SG90 Servo (at the entry and exit gate) and Firebase to create a real-time database connected to a web platform. The system provides real-time slot availability information via the web platform and LCD as information at the entrance gate. Users can easily make and cancel reservations with additional features such as OTP verification, and automatic booking cancellation have been successfully implemented. The prototype test method consist of calibration test, sending OTP test, automatic booking cancellation test and manual booking cancellation test. The result of calibration test on 10 cm range have a 80% success rate for ultrasonic sensor 1 as well as the result of ultrasonic sensor 2. While, additional features test result such as sending OTP, automatic booking cancellation, and manual booking cancellation having 100% success rate. It can be concluded that this prototype is successfully implemented and reach the goals with minimum error can be tolerated. The authors suggest to adding a keypad and payment system to this prototype for improvement in the future.

articleTitle: Blockchain Technology Model to Increase Transparency in the Distribution of Aid to Disaster Victims
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Indonesia is a country with a high potential for natural disasters. Almost every year in Indonesia, natural disasters such as floods, landslides, and other natural disasters occur. Several humanitarian organizations have taken the initiative to aid victims of natural disasters. The aid distribution process using conventional systems cannot provide transparent and accurate information on the distribution of aid to victims of natural disasters. Donors cannot find out information on the allocation of aid for disaster victims in real time and transparently because the system used uses a conventional approach. The next problem is that some parties misuse disaster relief fund. Thus, the problem statement of this research is blockchain technology can increase the transparency and accuracy of information on the distribution of aid to victims of natural disasters. The research uses a qualitative approach through a literature review to analyze the phenomena and problems surrounding the process of distributing aid to victims of natural disasters. A literature review was also carried out to study the concept of blockchain technology as an alternative solution to answer research problem statements. The research result is a model for adopting blockchain technology to increase transparency and security of information on aid distribution for victims of natural disasters and simulation using the Hyperledger framework.

articleTitle: Remaining Life Prediction of Transformers at Medium Voltage Distribution Substations Based on Load Curve
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Power transformers are electrical devices used in power distribution systems to increase (step-up) or decrease (step-down) the electrical voltage to suit the needs of electricity users. Transformers are very important in supporting human electricity needs. The increasing demand for electricity makes the continuity of electricity supply a top priority. Electricity supply is important to meet the increasing load demand. Meeting the increasing load demand requires a transformer with a long remaining life of 20.55 years according to the IEC 60076-7, 2005 standard. This study in determining the remaining life of the transformer uses a basis load curve. The remaining life of the transformer using the basis load curve has a remaining life of the transformer in 2023 24.48 years, 2024 23.51 years, and 2025 22.53 years. The remaining life requires a mitigation and maintenance process for the transformer in order to extend the remaining life of the transformer. A long remaining life can avoid excessive loading or oil contamination by outside air. Therefore, to avoid this, routine mitigation and maintenance are carried out to prevent damage or failure before more serious damage occurs.

Author Keywords: Transformer Remaining Life Prediction and IEC 60076-7

articleTitle: Optimizing Wall Materials to Reduce Electrical Energy Consumption of Building
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: The use of wall insulation is a crucial approach to mitigate electricity usage within a building, resulting in financial savings and a direct reduction in the release of atmospheric pollutants. The research goal was to assess the effect of various building wall materials on the cooling load, specifically in relation to air conditioning (AC). The objective of this work was to choose a certain style of wall and examine the impact of the AC load by utilizing different compositions of wall material. The kind of material as follow as: Styrofoam, soil, cement and alkalis. To achieved a high insulation of wall material, particle swarm optimization (PSO) has been applied to find optimal composition of material to create an Innovative Cellular Lightweight Concrete (Inn CLC) brick. A computational model for AC load has been devised to determine the electrical energy usage of a building. Two distinct types of walls have been constructed on the building, each with unique characteristics. A study reveals that the EC of building without and under Inn CLC brick CLC brick were: IDR 28.000 and IDR 17.500, respectively. Consequently, the saving energy consumption (EC) can be achieved to IDR 10,500.

articleTitle: Design of a 1000 W Boost Inverter Using The Sine Pulse Wave Modulation (SPWM) Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: An inverter is a device that converts DC power into AC power and is used to provide an alternative power source from batteries or accumulators when the main power source, such as the grid, is interrupted. There are two types of inverters, low frequency (LF) and high frequency (HF), each with advantages and disadvantages. LF inverters often experience decreased performance and power losses that cause voltage drops, so it is necessary to develop HF inverters for better efficiency. In this research, an HF inverter that produces pure sine waves and a stable voltage of 230 VAC, similar to the PLN voltage, is developed. The inverter is designed with two parts. First, a circuit to increase the voltage from 12 VDC to 380 VDC using a push-pull topology with a frequency of 50 kHz. Second, this circuit is then processed using the Sine Pulse Wave Modulation (SPWM) method to produce a pure sine wave after passing through the filter. The test results show that this inverter works well at a maximum load of 600W, the output voltage reaches 194V at an output current of 2.4A, while the input current is 54.18A. The efficiency of the inverter reaches 82%, with the wave produced being pure sine at a frequency of 50Hz.

articleTitle: Effective Model of Boost Converter Based on Simulink MATLAB
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: The boost converter is widely used in various DC-DC power conversion systems to step up the voltage from a direct current (DC) source. This paper presents a comparative study of a boost converter model implemented in Simulink using two approaches: mathematical equation-based modeling and a circuit-based model utilizing Simulink library components. The results show that the mathematical model produces an output voltage of 24.03V with a maximum overshoot of 90.5%, a steady-state time of 0.35s, and a conversion efficiency of 49%. In contrast, the circuit-based model delivers an output voltage of 23.14V, with a maximum overshoot of 81.5%, a steady-state time of 0.012s, and a conversion efficiency of 52%. The voltage regulation for the mathematical model is measured at 0.88%, while the circuit-based model achieves 0.82%. While the mathematical model provides a more accurate output voltage, it suffers from significant overshoot and a longer time to reach steady state. Conversely, the circuit-based model exhibits a faster transient response but less accurate voltage output. Additionally, the study highlights that the difference in switching components between the two models plays a crucial role in their performance. The mathematical model uses a simplified switch representation that focuses solely on ON/OFF transitions, which eases theoretical analysis. However, the circuit-based model incorporates a MOSFET, capturing more complex physical behaviors like internal resistance, capacitance, and switching losses, resulting in simulation outcomes that are closer to real-world conditions. This trade-off between simplicity and accuracy underlines the strengths and limitations of each approach in modeling the boost converter.

articleTitle: Implementing a Semi-Autonomous Robot for Ball Tracking in the University of Jember ABU Robot Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: The development of robotics technology is growing rapidly. Indonesian Robot Contest (Kontes Robot Indonesia - KRI) is a form of competition for developing robotics in Indonesia. This research develops a semi-autonomous robot that can perform robot missions semi-autonomously. The semi-autonomous ABU robot is designed with a ball object detection system using the Convolutional Neural Network method of yolov5 algorithm consisting of 213 layers. Before the implementation of the detection, a model is obtained after the training process, which requires 2,500 training image data and 353 testing data with a hyperparameter of 100 epochs and 24 batches. The process produces a model with a mAP value of 0.850. The detection system can achieve a detection accuracy value of 78.3% - 100% in offline and real-time testing with differences in object distance and light intensity when detecting objects. Then, in the object tracking system accompanied by robot movements that have been tested 10 times with different angular ranges of objects, the average travel time is 2.27 seconds to reach the object's center point.

articleTitle: Detection and Identification of RBC Abnormalities in Essential Thrombocythemia Patients Using ResNet50V2
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: The MPN condition has been observed to present with several abnormalities in RBCs, including an increased RBC count and alterations in RBC shape. The elevated number of red blood cells (RBCs) in ET is responsible for the increased viscosity, which subsequently reduces the velocity of blood flow. The initial examination for early detection is a full blood count (FBC) but cannot exclude an increase in the number and variation of red blood cells (RBC). A limitation of the FBC examination is failure to detect cell morphological abnormalities, requiring instead microscopic examination of peripheral blood smears. Furthermore, microscopic examinations implemented in hospital laboratories are still performed manually by clinical pathologists. It is evident that the manual examination is inherently subjective, dependent on the clinical pathologist's experience. It is essential to develop a technological solution that enables the identification of RBC shape abnormalities through the application of computer vision to facilitate the work of clinical pathologists. The objective of this study is to apply the ResNet-50V2 algorithm to the classification of red blood cell (RBC) abnormalities in patients with essential thrombocythemia. The model effectively classified five classes of RBCs (normal erythrocytes, elliptocytes, ovalocytes, stomatocytes and teardrops) with the highest accuracy of 95% at a learning rate of 0.001 and a maximum iteration of 50 epochs.

articleTitle: A Compact Circular Filtering Antenna for C-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: In this paper, a compact circular filtering antenna for C-band application is presented. It comprises four main parts, including a circular patch with a U-shaped cutout at the bottom, inserted feeding, a half circle resonator with two curved arms, and a feeding microstrip line. The proposed circular filtering antenna has a size of 30 x 25 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with a thickness of 1.67 mm. It has two nulls that represent the filter’s stopband at a lower frequency of 4.8 GHz and a higher frequency of 5.4 GHz. Additionally, the filter passband is presented by a max gain of 6.2 dBi at the center frequency of 5 GHz. Furthermore, the filter function is also shown by the surface current distribution at frequencies of 4.8 GHz, 5 GHz, and 5.4 GHz. Based on the simulated results, the strongest surface current distribution occurs in the radiator patch at a frequency of 5 GHz, while the strongest surface current distribution happens in the insert feeding at frequencies of 4.8 GHz and 5.4 GHz. The simulated result of impedance bandwidth (IBW) is achieved around 550 MHz, spanning from 4.83 GHz to 5.38 GHz. Next, it has a 3 dB beamwidth of 97° with the mainlobe at 6°. For C-band applications, the proposed circular filtering antenna has good filter function characteristics.

articleTitle: Battery Charger with Bridgeless Power Factor Correction using PID-ANN Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: This paper presents a control scheme for a proportional–integral–derivative (PID) controller combined with an artificial neural network (ANN) for a battery charger bridgeless power factor correction (BPFC) Cuk converter. The BPFC Cuk converter eliminates the diode bridge, functioning as a multifunction converter capable of stepping up and stepping down output voltage. To maintain a constant output voltage, an effective control system must be implemented. The PID controller is a widely used technique due to its simplicity; however, it performs poorly in nonlinear applications. This paper proposes a combination of PID and ANN controllers for the BPFC Cuk converter to address the limitations of conventional PID control, particularly during transient operation. The proposed PID-ANN controller's effectiveness is analyzed with three different output voltages: -42 V, -48 V, and -54 V. The characteristics of the battery charger BPFC output during start-up, including overshoot voltage, undershoot voltage, and settling time, are examined. Results are verified using MATLAB-Simulink simulation, demonstrating that the proposed PID-ANN controller effectively controls the output voltage and achieves improved performance during the Cuk converter's start-up.

articleTitle: Modern AI Technique Development For Fault Detection And Analysis On Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: The reliable and efficient operation of distribution networks is critical for modern power systems but increasing complexity and integration of distributed generation introduce novel uncertainties, leading to potential faults. This paper explores the application of Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) and Support Vector Machines (SVM) for fault detection and analysis within the IEEE 33 bus system. Both AI techniques were developed and trained using historical fault data, followed by a comparative analysis based on accuracy and confusion matrices. The ANN model demonstrated higher accuracy, achieving training and testing accuracies of 88.9517% and 88.3592%, respectively, but struggled to distinguish between single-line-to-ground (SLG) and double-line-to-ground (DLG) faults. In contrast, the SVM model achieved lower accuracies of 60.9123% (training) and 59.4459% (testing), with significant misclassifications across all fault types. The strengths and weaknesses of each approach are discussed, highlighting the ANN model's robustness and computational demands and the SVM model's efficiency in high-dimensional spaces but sensitivity to hyperparameter tuning. This study provides valuable insights into optimizing AI techniques for fault detection, aiming to enhance the reliability and efficiency of distribution networks.

articleTitle: Optimal Placement of Insertion Transformers in Distribution system
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: One of the most frequent problems in distribution system planning is determining the location of the insert transformer. Determining the location of the insert transformer has bring impact on network efficiency in the distribution system. This research aims to optimize the placement of insert transformers to reduce overload, increase voltage and reduce losses in the distribution system. To achieved the aim of this research, genetic algorithm as applied to define the optimal placement of transformer insertion in distribution system. In this research, there were 3 distribution substations that were analyzed, called KMO 177, KMO 218 and KMO 219. Based on this research indicated that the overload and losses can be reduced and the voltage can be increased. For KMO 177, overload decreased from 89.3% to be 50.1%, the voltage increased from 384 Volt to be 391 Volt and the losses can be reduced from 1.23 kW to be 0.31 kW. For KMO 218, overload decreased from 85.3% to be 49.5%, the voltage increased from 370 Volt to be 383 Volt and the losses can be reduced from 1.45 kW to be 0.39 kW. Similarly, overload decreased from 88.9% to be 54.8%, the voltage increased from 378 Volt to be 385 Volt and the losses can be reduced from 1.70 kW to be 0.46 kW for KMO 219. This research is applied in Kotamobagu, North Sulawesi-Indonesia.

articleTitle: New Design of Wideband Antenna with Two-and-a-Half Circular Patch for C-Band Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Long-distance communication requires an antenna design with wideband characteristics. A wideband antenna can receive a broad range of frequencies, and one type of antenna that supports satellite communication systems is the microstrip antenna. A microstrip antenna, designed with two half-circular patches, can operate optimally at frequencies between 4.5 GHz and 8.4 GHz with a bandwidth of 4000 MHz. Using two half-circular patches proves more effective in return loss simulations, achieving optimal results down to -25 dB. Circular-shaped patches can significantly increase the bandwidth compared to rectangular patches. The antenna dimensions need to be adjusted to precisely align the operating frequency within the 4 GHz to 8 GHz range. It should also be noted that the antenna dimensions will increase if the operating frequency needs to be shifted.

articleTitle: Positioning System for the Roadheader based on UWB-IMU
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: To enhance the efficiency and promote green mining in coal extraction, while advancing intelligent and unmanned operations for coal mining equipment, achieving breakthroughs in key intelligent technologies for the roadheader—a critical piece of mining equipment—becomes particularly essential. Regarding the concept of "green mining" in this context, it refers to reducing environmental impact by improving the precision and efficiency of equipment operations, thereby minimizing unnecessary energy consumption and resource waste. In underground tunnels, the Ultra-Wide Band and Inertial Measurement Unit systems commonly used for roadheader positioning each have distinct strengths and limitations. To address significant roll and pitch errors due to multipath and non-line-of-sight issues, as well as the low positioning accuracy resulting from IMU heading drift, this study proposes a positioning fusion method based on Time of Arrival that combines UWB and IMU data. By leveraging the high-precision roll and pitch angles obtained from the IMU, this approach aims to refine the UWB-calculated positioning results. To investigate the feasibility of this fusion method, experiments were conducted on the forward and backward movements of a boom-type roadheader within a simulated tunnel environment. Additionally, using a total station, the global coordinate system was established by measuring the distances between four UWB base stations and four UWB tags. Using the Newton iteration method, the roadheader’s pose was directly calculated, with attitude updates achieved by incorporating the changes in IMU- derived roll and pitch angles. Experimental results indicate that the fusion of IMU roll and pitch angle increments into UWB- based positioning systems significantly enhances positioning accuracy. This study’s positioning fusion method contributes to green mining by ensuring more accurate and stable positioning of roadheaders, which in turn supports precise, efficient tunneling and resource extraction.

articleTitle: Distribution System Enhancement Based on Power Electronics Converter with Corona Herd Immunity Optimizer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Electric distribution systems are a platform where consumers finally get power for loads. Enhancing the performance of a distribution system is a strategy that is continuously updated due to the vast changes its enduring. In this work, the enhancement of such a system is implemented by connection of back to back converters at certain buses. Since these converters deliver controlled power flow at the points of connections, a key challenge is finding the values of such powers. In this work, an optimization process is formulated to find the optimal values of controlled power for the converter set. The approach is based on a recently developed Corona Herd Immunity optimizer (CHIO) that reflects the COVID 2019 epidemic. This optimizer adopts solutions for populations that have gained immunity as a result of infection. The CHIO is implemented on a test distribution with the objective of reducing active power losses. Results proves the proficiency and reliability of CHIO in obtaining solutions with minimal losses that can raise the efficiency of the system. Simulations carried out in MATLAB adopted several locations of converters position with and without distributed generation connection.

articleTitle: Enhancing Traffic Signs Recognition Systems Through Gabor Feature Extraction Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: The traffic sign image recognition system is one of the essential elements required by an autonomous vehicle, where these signs also serve as a guide for the autonomous car. Images of traffic signs will be captured by cameras on uncrewed vehicles. These images will then be processed for recognition, where the features in the traffic sign images will be extracted to obtain a characteristic for each traffic sign. Some of the obstacles that exist are the condition of traffic signs, such as changing color due to exposure to heat and rain, variations in lighting on traffic signs that occur at night and during the day, and also the various shapes of these traffic signs that must be considered when carrying out extraction. The features are round, rhombus, and square traffic signs. In this research, a method for extracting traffic sign image features has been developed using HSV and Wavelet Gabor. HSV obtains a sign image (region of interest) from the existing image. In contrast, Wavelet Gabor is used to recognize the type of sign detected. This research used a database of 20 kinds of signs with round, rhombus, and square shapes. The traffic sign image recognition system using Gabor wavelet as a feature extractor achieved an accuracy of 93.33% and 100% accuracy at night time.

articleTitle: Development A Microstrip Antenna Array with 8 Elements and Dolph-Chebyshev Distribution for Capturing Signals from the Himawari-8 Satellite
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: This research presents a concept for a linear microstrip antenna array with rectangular elements, intended to serve as the feed antenna for a parabolic reflector system at ground stations receiving data from the Himawari-8 satellite. The device`s antenna is engineered to operate within frequencies between 3.8 and 4.2 GHz. The design of a linear array microstrip antenna was modeled using CST Microwave Studio software. The antenna was constructed on a Rogers RT/Duroid-5880 substrate, which has a thickness of 1.575 mm and a dielectric constant of 2.2. This research using various approaches and strategies are employed, including the proximity couple feed method, corporate feed approach, Dolph-Chebyshev technique, Wilkinson unequal power divider procedure, and parabolic reflector system. A 1×8 linear array antenna design was modeled, resulting in the following performance characteristics a bandwidth of 721.9 MHz operating between 3.7069 and 4.4288 GHz, a peak gain at 16.17 dB at 4.148 GHz, a horizontal half-power beamwidth (HPBW) of 6.5°, a vertical HPBW of 46.5°, and a directional radiation pattern. The 1×8 linear array antenna, when used as feed for 2.4-meter parabolic reflector, achieves the following performance characteristics a bandwidth of 721.9 MHz, spanning from 3.7069 to 4.4288 GHz, a peak gain of 30.69 dB at 4.148 GHz, half-power beamwidth (HPBW) of 7.7° horizontally and 1.4° vertically, and directional radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Message Queuing Telemetry Transport Utilization for Internet of Things-Based Document Locker Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: In certain cases, the digitalization of important governmental documents is undergoing rapid development, but many documents still require official hard copies, which are tedious to obtain in addition to requiring face-to-face contact. Leveraging Internet of Things (IoT) and Message Queueing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) technology, the objective of this research is to develop a locker system to store sensitive documents in key spots, controlled with a simple and intuitive system, facilitating streamlined access to documents while minimizing the need for physical visits to centralized offices, thereby promoting reduced face-to-face interactions. This is achieved by using a WeMOS D1 R32 unit and a 16-channel relay controlling a series of solenoid door locks, listening to messages sent in an MQTT topic. General maintainability of the device is suboptimal, requiring further research and development.

articleTitle: Optimizing of Protection Coordination Overcurrent Relay Using Adaptive Modified Firefly Algorithm in Gases Industrial
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Protection coordination has an active support power in an electric power system for system reliability, recognizing abnormal conditions, and selective properties to isolate disturbances so that they do not spread, thus securing other equipment. The use of overcurrent relay in electrical network systems is due to its fast response characteristics, flexible protection coordination settings, and optimization between the main and backup relays to avoid protection failure. This paper, using Adaptive Modified Firefly Algorithm (AMFA) optimization method is used to obtain the optimal overcurrent relays value in the electrical network system. The AMFA method aims to obtain the optimal Time Dial Setting (TDS) value so that the total operating time can be faster and more precise accurating of time to insulated trouble with implementation using MATLAB and ETAP software to simulate the results. The results confirm that relay 9 has a primary time to operate of 0.1009s and a secondary operating time of 0.0000s, confirming that the performance time gap between the secondary and primary relays remains within 0.2s. As well, relays R.P2.CF3.F5, R.P2.CF3.F2, and R.P2.CF1.F2 showcase identical total primary and secondary operating times, calculated as 0.1009s, 0.3013s, and 0.4961s.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Co-firing in a Pulverized Coal Boiler Using Multi-Biomass: Sawdust and Rice Husks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: This study investigates the impact of co-firing biomass with coal at Pulverized Coal (PC) Boiler-type power plant. While fossil fuels, particularly coal, continue to dominate global energy production, they significantly contribute to greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Despite efforts to reduce coal-fired power generation capacity in Indonesia, coal remains a major component of the country's energy mix. To support the government's renewable energy goals and reduce GHG emissions, biomass co-firing is being explored as a viable solution. Various biomass types, including saw dust, rice husks, cocopeat, and palm shells, were evaluated for their potential in co-firing applications. Unlike other studies that utilize a single type of biomass, this study employs multiple biomass types, specifically sawdust and rice husks. The use of multi-biomass offers an alternative solution to the challenge of biomass feedstock availability. This research assesses both the technical and economic feasibility of biomass co-firing, with a focus on gross calorific value (GCV), Hardgrove Grindability Index (HGI), generation cost and emissions reduction. Laboratory tests and combustion modeling were conducted to analyze the performance and environmental impacts. The results indicate that biomass co-firing can effectively reduce emissions while maintaining operational performance, positioning it as a promising strategy for sustainable energy production in Indonesia. In this paper, the authors aim to explore the impact of biomass utilization as a co-firing material in a PC Boiler power plant.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of 5 kWp Floating PV at Puspiptek Serpong Lake
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Floating PV is a renewable energy developed in Indonesia, as an alternative to reduce the need for large land areas by using the water surface to place PV panels. One of the FPVs operating in Indonesia is located in Lake Puspiptek Serpong. The on-grid system with a capacity of 5.36 kWp, supplies electricity to the Bahrul Ulum Mosque during the day. The purpose of this research is to analyze the performance of the 5kWp floating FPV of Lake Puspiptek Serpong. The analysis was carried out by determining the values of Yr (Yield References), Yf (Yield Factor), PR (Performance Ratio) and CF (Capacity Factor) obtained from the results of real measurements carried out for 4 months compared to the results of the Pvsyst simulation. The results of real measurements obtained Yr, Yf, PR and CF values of 3.692; 2.167; 61.23% and 9.39%, respectively. Lower than the Pvsyst simulation results of 4.899; 3.984; 81.57% and 16.68% respectively. The difference in results is caused by the FPV system having an energy limiter, installed according to national electricity regulations that work to limit the distribution of electrical energy following the amount of load used (zero export). As a result, PV performance is not optimal because the irradiation received by the PV is not all channeled into electrical energy. Based on the PR value obtained, the FPV of Puspiptek Serpong Lake has good performance.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Lithium Polymer Pack and Lithium Ion Pack Batteries With Load Variations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Batteries are the main device in electronic devices. Batteries have developed rapidly to become the main energy source for modern vehicles, namely electric cars. Lithium-ion batteries are lithium batteries with electrolytes in gel form inside. This battery is widely found in everyday life because it has one of the best energy densities, has no memory effect, and experiences a slow loss of content when not in use. Lithium polymer batteries are different from lithium ion, lithium polymer batteries use dry electrolytes in the form of layers and layers. A data logger is a monitoring system designed to store and monitor real-time data in the form of voltage, current, and time. The performance of the 48 V 6.6 Ah polymer lithium battery pack against varying 5A current loading results in an average current usage of 5.03 A. The temperature rise that occurred during the test with 5A current was 1.10°C and the battery experienced a power loss of 25.7 watts. The performance of a 48 V 6AH lithium-ion pack battery against a 5A current loading variation resulted in an average current of 5.03 A. The temperature increase that occurred during the test with a 5A current was 5.8°C with a residual voltage of 44.27 volts. Tests that have been carried out show that the battery will experience a faster and greater discharge when the discharging capacity is also high. The polymer lithium battery shows a decrease in intensity of 39 watts when tested with a variation of 7A current and the capacity used is 3.65Ah. The lithium-ion battery shows a power reduction of 68.7 watts with a used capacity of 3.51 Ah at 7A of varying current loading

articleTitle: Virtual Reality Exposure Therapy as a Novel Approach to Acrophobia Treatment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Acrophobia, or the fear of heights, is a common anxiety disorder that significantly impacts daily functioning and quality of life. Traditional treatment methods, such as cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), have demonstrated some success, but they often require considerable time and resources. This study investigates the efficacy of Virtual Reality Exposure Therapy (VRET) as an alternative treatment for acrophobia. Using immersive virtual environments, VRET provides controlled and safe exposure to height-related scenarios, allowing individuals to confront and manage their fears. Participants were randomly assigned to either a VRET group or a CBT control group, and their acrophobia symptoms were measured before and after treatment using the Acrophobia Questionnaire (AQ). The results showed a significant reduction in anxiety and avoidance behaviors in the VRET group, with an average decrease in AQ scores of 49.6 points, compared to a minimal change of 1.07 points in the control group. These findings suggest that VRET is a highly effective treatment for acrophobia, offering a viable and innovative alternative to traditional therapeutic methods. The paper concludes by discussing the implications for clinical practice and future research directions.

articleTitle: Implementation of Robot Navigation Based on Artificial Potential Field for a Four Omni-directional Soccer Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: The Indonesian Robot Contest (KRI) is an event by the National Achievement Centre, emphasizing design and engineering. The Indonesian Wheeled Robot Soccer Contest is among its divisions, where robots compete to score goals while adhering to rules penalizing collisions. To tackle this, an additional algorithm utilizing the potential field method is crucial for penalty avoidance. It is adept at maneuvering around static and dynamic obstacles, fitting the soccer robot's needs. The potential field algorithm was successfully implemented on OMR kinematics with a coordinate error of less than 3%. Researchers tested static and dynamic obstacles to test the repulsive potential field. For static obstacles, the robot reached the target point with an error of less than 1%, successfully avoiding all collisions and demonstrating the system's reliability in performing its task. For dynamic obstacles, the robot could move to the target point with an error of less than 6%, with collisions occurring in 2 out of 10 trials. The average failure to avoid collisions was primarily due to poor obstacle detection by the image processing system

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Wavelet Transform-Based Robust Reversible Watermarking Using Adaptive Spread Spectrum Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: In the digital era, data security has become a critical concern due to the increasing prevalence of threats like unauthorized access, modification, and forgery. Watermarking techniques have emerged as an effective means to safeguard digital images by embedding additional information, such as ownership details or authentication codes, within the image. However, ensuring that the image's quality and integrity remain intact while embedding a watermark is particularly challenging, especially in sensitive fields like healthcare and military, where any form of image degradation is unacceptable. This study presents a comparative analysis of robust reversible watermarking techniques based on wavelet transforms, using Adaptive Spread Spectrum (ASS) methods. The approach incorporates both Haar Wavelet Transform (HWT) and Integer Wavelet Transform (IWT) to embed and extract the watermark. During the process, the image is decomposed into four sub-bands, and the watermark is embedded into the low-frequency (LL) sub-band, which typically preserves more image details. Experimental results show that the proposed method significantly improves resistance to various types of attacks, including JPEG compression, noise, and rotation, while maintaining a BER of 0 in the LL sub-band and high PSNR values. The watermarking system effectively safeguards copyright and image integrity using the HWT scheme and LL sub-band, further enhancements are required to improve its robustness against more complex attacks. This makes the approach ideal for applications where both high security and minimal image distortion are required.

articleTitle: Optimizing Service Deployments With NLP Based Infrastructure Code Generation - An Automation Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: In this paper we discuss how we combine natural language processing (NLP) techniques and infrastructure as code (IaC) tools like Terraform; to build a framework that converts natural language queries into Terraform code, enabling users to generate multi-cloud infrastructure configurations. We detail the construction of the NLP engine, the implementation for benchmarking various context-aware models, and the validation and execution of code, which leads to the integration of the model with DevSecOps pipelines. For benchmarking, we test models such as RoBERTa, GPT-4, T5 and Llama on their performance in terms of accuracy, latency and capacity to translate complex infrastructure requirements given as conversational queries into deployable terraform configuration. On one hand, this framework enhances the accessibility and efficiency of writing Terraform code (TF-code), while on the other, it results in a 73% reduction in the overall time required to bring a service from development to production deployment, relative to comparable efforts performed through manual processes. This modularity allows the entire framework to be customized and integrated into larger systems, especially in a DevSecOps context where flexibility and extensibility are crucial. Finally, the paper provides both technical insights and practical benchmarks, offering a comprehensive solution for organizations seeking to optimize cloud service deployment pipelines using advanced NLP techniques.

articleTitle: The Application of Cowrie Honeypot to Analyze Attacks on SSH and Telnet Protocols
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: The advancement of Internet technologies has led to growing security threats due to vulnerabilities in information systems. Various security solutions have been developed to counter these threats, but they often struggle to keep pace with increasingly sophisticated attack strategies. This study examines the effectiveness of a Cowrie honeypot system for analyzing SSH protocol attacks. By deploying Cowrie on a Raspberry Pi over 30 days, detailed data on attacker behavior was gathered. Key findings reveal the predominance of SSH over Telnet attacks, frequent targeting of weak passwords, and a geographic concentration of attacks from China, India, and Australia. This study underscores the need for robust password policies and user education to reduce vulnerabilities. Cowrie proved valuable in capturing comprehensive logs and providing critical insights into attacker strategies, highlighting the importance of incorporating honeypots into cybersecurity infrastructure.

articleTitle: Comparative Performance Analysis of Decision Tree and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) Algorithms for Malformed Food Aroma Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: One example of a significant food industry in Indonesia is the tofu industry. Tofu is very popular and has high nutritional value. However, the emergence of serious issues related to the use of hazardous materials such as formalin in food has become a serious threat to public health. Therefore, it is important to prevent the use of formalin in tofu production to protect the consumers’ health. This study aims to classify the aroma quality of tofu preserved with formalin based on its chemical components. The classification methods utilize k-nearest neighbors (kNN) and Decision Tree (DT). Evaluation of classification results using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score metrics. The experimental results with the Formalin Tofu Aroma dataset showed that KNN has 80.86% accuracy, 72.04% precision, 99.05% recall, and 83.44% F1-score. Meanwhile, the Decision Tree has 75.17% accuracy, 75.85% precision, 71.73% recall, and 73.70% F1-score. Based on these results, KNN is superior in terms of accuracy, recall, and F1 score. Whereas the Decision Tree outperforms in terms of precision.

articleTitle: Water Quality Monitoring System Using Wireless Sensor Network Using Automatic Solar Tracker
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Water plays a crucial role in human life and agricultural activities. Monitoring key parameters such as pH and temperature is essential for maintaining water quality, as they affect nutrient availability, disease resistance, and environmental balance. This study develops a wireless water quality monitoring system using pH and temperature sensors, powered by solar energy with an automatic solar tracker. The system includes two sensor nodes placed at different points in an irrigation channel, communicating via Bluetooth and LoRa-Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) to a server for real-time data display. The solar tracker improves energy efficiency, ensuring continuous system operation. Initial tests demonstrated an average error rate of 1.5% for pH measurements and less than 1% for temperature measurements. The system also showed a 15% increase in power output with the solar tracker compared to a static solar panel. Future improvements will focus on sensor calibration and the integration of additional parameters such as dissolved oxygen for a more comprehensive water quality assessment.

articleTitle: Development of Gamification-Based Web Programming Educational Website with Peer Review to Increase Student Learning Motivation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Web programming is a crucial subject for class XI RPL students at SMKN 12 Malang, but many struggle due to a lack of engaging teaching materials, leading to low motivation. To address this, the study develops a gamification-based web programming teaching website with peer review features. The research uses the R&D method and the Design Thinking model, which includes five stages: empathy, definition, ideation, prototyping, and testing. The study involves Material and Media Experts for product validation and students for trials and deployment. The goal of this study's output is instructional media for Web Programming that is useful and accessible to students at any time and location. By utilizing gamification and peer review, this website is anticipated to boost students' motivation to learn and encourage collaboration amongst peers as they work through the material. Results of the feasibility validation process include: (1) media expert validation an 88.18% percentage in the good category and (2) material validation an 89.92% percentage in the very good category. Twenty-five students from class XI RPL SMKN 12 Malang have implemented media use. (3) A percentage of 84.67% with good criteria was shown by the user trial findings. (4) The student learning motivation test's findings revealed a very high criterion percentage of 82.69%. This demonstrates how the use of gamification can increase students' motivation to learn. Students, material experts, and media specialists have evaluated the viability of the gamification-based learning resources. As a result, the media is considered practicable and appropriate for use as a learning support medium in the Web Programming courses of Vocational High Schools..

articleTitle: Optimizing Energy Efficiency in Smart Grids Through Wireless Communication and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Energy efficiency is a critical requirement for nations across the globe. In this connection, Smart Grids (SGs) have become a focal point due to the integration of numerous sensors and modern hardware, including smart devices. This research investigates the optimization of energy efficiency in smart grid systems by enhancing wireless communication through advanced machine learning algorithms. Moreover, this study explores the Home Area Networks (HANs) technologies such as ZigBee, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, 6LoWPAN, and Z-Wave within the SG context. We propose a model to streamline data transmission, improve reliability, and strengthen security measures. Python-based simulations will be conducted to evaluate the model's efficacy, with results presented through various graphical representations. Through the integration of deep learning model, 99% accuracy, 98% precision and 97% recall was achieved. Preliminary results indicate that the integration of machine learning techniques significantly enhances energy optimization.

articleTitle: Skincare Recommendation System based on User’s Skin Characteristics Similarity using Collaborative Filtering Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: In order to obtain the optimal result from skincare products, consumer must use the ones that are suitable for their skin. However, the large amount of skincare products that are available in the market might cause confusion to consumer in choosing the right skincare products for themselves. Therefore, this study proposes a skincare recommendation system that will provide skincare product recommendations to consumer based on their skin characteristics. The proposed model will implement collaborative filtering approach by finding other consumer with similar skin characteristics using cosine similarity method, read-through the review comments to determine the rating of the products and create the relationship between users and products using Singular Vector Decomposition (SVD) algorithm. As a result, the proposed model shows an excellent result with accuracy score of 92.8%, highest among all baseline models. The proposed model also successfully outperformed other system that employed different approach with precision score of 76%. Hence, it is proven that the proposed model can give better skincare product recommendation to consumer.

articleTitle: Student Academic Prediction Based on Alcohol Consumption Level Using Random Forest Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Alcohol consumption is a serious social problem, especially among students, due to ease of access and lack of supervision from parents and educators. Alcohol consumption has a negative impact, especially on students, directly or indirectly. Based on a 2015 study, 112 (66%) out of 170 students did not attend classes or failed exams due to alcohol intoxication. It proves that the level of alcohol consumption impacts students’ academic performance. Therefore, it is necessary to predict students’ academic performance to minimize the adverse effects of alcohol consumption. A method to predict academic performance is data mining. This research consists of 5 stages: literature review, data collection, data pre-processing, data processing, and evaluation. The data is obtained from the public dataset "Student Alcohol Consumption", which includes variables such as grades in the first, second and third semesters, demographic aspects, academic aspects, family aspects, social aspects of students, and the alcohol consumption of students on weekdays and weekends. The data pre-processing stage involves several processes, including discretization, set role, and Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) upsampling. The prediction model used to diagnose students’ academic performance was the random forest. The prediction results are evaluated using accuracy, precision, and recall metrics. The results demonstrated that Random Forest produced the best results on the Portuguese language dataset using SMOTE and two-class labels with 95.54% accuracy, 98.08% precision, and 92.90% recall. Based on these results, it can be concluded that the Random Forest algorithm is good for predicting student performance based on their alcohol consumption levels using two-class labels and balanced data. So, this algorithm can help schools mitigate the influence of alcohol on student’s academics.

articleTitle: Applying Conflict-Based Search to Improve Pathfinding Efficiency in Multi-Agent Big Data Adventure Games
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: The implementation of intelligent pathfinding algorithms is essential for improving gameplay experience and educational value in educational games. This study looks into applying conflict-based search for multi-agent pathfinding in an educational game called "Data Quest: Big Data Adventure," intended for active learning in teaching big data concepts. Conflict-based Search (CBS) optimizes pathfinding and conflict resolution through multi-agent coordination, thereby improving real-time responsiveness and educational engagement. CBS enhances real-time response and education. The results show that compared with conventional approaches such as cooperative A*, CBS reduces the computation time of pathfinding by 30-50% in medium to high-density environments and achieves a conflict resolution efficiency of 75% to 85% in the first iteration. The generated paths by CBS are nearly optimal, differing by only 5-10% from ideal paths, which is adequate in educational scenarios. The successful application of CBS not only enhances the performance of multi-agent interactions but also underscores the importance of integrating advanced AI techniques in educational gaming, paving the way for more immersive and effective learning experiences. These results show how well CBS can enable dynamic and complex interaction within an educational game, highlighting its potential for broader educational applications that benefit from advanced AI-driven, multi-agent systems.

articleTitle: Literature Review of Hybrid Propulsion System on Ship
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: The International Maritime Organization (IMO), the regulatory authority for shipping worldwide, has introduced regulations to curb ship emissions. Following attempts to reduce emissions by slowing down ships, which can compromise maneuverability, research into alternative solutions has intensified. One such area of focus is hybrid power sources and propulsion systems. These systems can be configured in three primary architectures: series, parallel, and a combination of both. Hybrid propulsion specifically refers to systems with parallel or series-parallel architectures. Research into hybrid propulsion remains relatively limited due to current constraints that hinder its widespread adoption across all vessel types. Even though, hybrid propulsion can allow ships to sailing and maneuvering safely and reduce exhaust gases. Research that has been carried out is related to hybrid propulsion, such as control systems and designs that can be applied to yachts, cruise ships, offshore supply vessels (OSVs), oceangoing vessels and fish ship. Implementing hybrid propulsion requires a careful evaluation of the benefits and drawbacks associated with each architectural configuration. The best architecture is a serial-parallel combination because it has high flexibility so it can produce comfortable conditions with low emissions and noise but still maintains performance for sailing and maneuvering.

articleTitle: A 1200 Wp Solar Powered Smart Microgrid Implementation for Practical Education Purposes in Semarang
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: In recent times, the reliance on fossil fuels as an energy source remains significantly high. The centralized nature of fossil fuel-based energy production, managed far from communities due to national security and stability factors, has seemingly left behind the shadow of energy crises as experienced in many countries. Nevertheless, the global awareness of alternative energy from green sources appears to be an intriguing trend to explore, considering Indonesia’s promising diversity and availability of green energy. This needs to be managed and utilized as a preemptive effort by creating an alternative energy production system. Distributed Energy Resources is one concept that can be a solution in realizing national energy resilience, starting from a local scale, in this case, specifically discussing solar-powered microgrids. However, a good, brief, and relevant solar microgrid educational module still hard to find in Semarang City. A simple module with SCADA system should be made to maintain the module relevance and to be a solution for the related issue. Through this writing, the author describes the model and operation of implementing a microgrid system for educational purposes and to build awareness of the importance of resilience in the energy sector. The implemented system itself, already meets the current technology demand with IOT capability to provide inter network tele-measuring and tele-controlling knowledge.
