This 1200 Wp capacity system successfully tested at KODAM IV/Diponegoro with all operation modes and SCADA concept implementation to provide intelligible module for education.

articleTitle: Evaluating Compliance of of the XYZ Ministry’s Android Messaging Applications with OWASP MASVS: A Comprehensive Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Safeguarding the security of government communication tools is crucial for protecting sensitive information. This study presents a thorough case analysis that assesses the compliance of the XYZ Ministry's Android messaging app with the OWASP Mobile Application Security Verification Standard (MASVS). OWASP MASVS offers a robust framework for evaluating the security stance of mobile applications, encompassing vital areas such as data protection, authentication, and network security. The study applied the OWASP MASVS standard to the XYZ Ministry's messaging application using automated and manual testing approaches to gauge adherence to security standards. Specifically, the research concentrated on MASVS-NETWORK-2 security controls. The primary goal of this research was to uncover vulnerabilities, evaluate compliance, and put forth actionable recommendations for enhancing application security. The findings indicated that the tested application failed to meet two of the five test sections in MASVS-NETWORK-2. The recommended course of action is to modify the code in Network Security Settings to accept certificates from the system exclusively.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Solar Panel System Failure Detection Using Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and AdaBoost
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: This research applies a combination of machine learning methods - Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and AdaBoost - to detect solar panel system failures using historical data. The ensemble model developed achieved an accuracy rate of 98.17 percent, with the best performance shown in Class 1 which achieved perfect scores (Precision, Recall, and F1-Score = 1.0000). Meanwhile, Class 0 and Class 2 also show excellent performance with Precision, Recall and F1-Score values above 0.96. These results prove that combining algorithms in an ensemble model produces higher detection accuracy than using a single algorithm, and can increase operational efficiency and maintenance of solar panel systems.

articleTitle: Integrating Big Data Concepts into Education Through RPG Games: A Study Using Agile Methodologies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: The incorporation of big data principles into educational programs is becoming increasingly vital in the context of Industry 4.0. Vocational high schools face considerable challenges in imparting these abstract concepts, primarily due to insufficient interactive learning tools. This paper details the development and evaluation of Data Quest: Big Data Adventure, an educational game aimed at improving students' comprehension of big data. Based on constructivist learning theory and gamification principles, this game was developed utilizing agile methodologies and evaluated with 23 students at SMKN 10 Malang. Surveys and questionnaires were conducted post-gameplay sessions to assess students' engagement and motivation levels. The tools gathered quantitative and qualitative data, offering insights into the game's impact on students' attitudes towards learning Big Data. The media validation results demonstrated a high potential effectiveness of 96%, usability of 84%, and satisfaction of 100%. Field tests indicated significant engagement, evidenced by high scores in accomplishment (84.51%), challenge (86.43%), competition (88.24%), guidance (87.57%), and social experience (85.57%). Immersion and playfulness achieved scores of 81.43% and 84.57%, respectively, indicating the game's effectiveness in engaging student interest. Results regarding student motivation were favourable, with scores recorded as follows: attention (80.80%), relevance (80%), confidence (78.43%), and satisfaction (81.43%). The findings indicate that gamified educational tools, such as Data Quest, can substantially improve big data literacy and motivation in vocational students. The interactive design and competitive elements enhance engagement, rendering abstract big data concepts more comprehensible and cultivating essential skills required for the data-driven needs of the industry 4.0 workforce.

articleTitle: Information Security Management Evaluation at ABC University Using OCTAVE-S and ISO Standards
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: ABC University, recognized as one of the leading educational institutions in Indonesia, bears significant responsibility for safeguarding its information security, mainly due to its reliance on technology to manage critical financial and educational data. Despite the university’s esteemed academic reputation, no prior research has evaluated the effectiveness of the information security practices implemented by the Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Unit. This study aims to fill this gap by assessing the Information Security Management System (ISMS) within the ICT unit, utilizing ISO 27001 standards in conjunction with the comprehensive risk evaluation framework of the OCTAVE-S method. Through qualitative methods—including interviews, document analysis, and field studies—this research identifies 15 security practice areas, revealing that 10 are rated red, 5 yellow, and none green. These findings indicate significant vulnerabilities in critical assets, such as the Academic Information System and Course Management System, which face 24 and 26 potential threats, respectively. By proposing risk mitigation measures across five key areas, this research enhances overall security at ABC University. Applying the Standar Nasional Indonesia (SNI) ISO 27001:2013 framework to develop tailored strategies for addressing identified threats protects sensitive financial and educational data and further reinforces ABC University’s credibility as a model of best practices in information security at the Indonesia University level.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Electronic Circuit System in Smart Aquaponic
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Aquaponics is a combination of plant cultivation and fish cultivation. This system continuously uses air from the fish farm for plants, then returns it to the fish pond. The basic principle of this system is to provide optimal air for each raw material through a circulation system and using advanced technology to make human work easier. This research evaluates the electronic circuit system needed to assess the power requirements for producing vegetables and fish through aquaponics. Some supporting tools are Solar Cells to convert sunlight energy into electrical energy, DS1820b sensors to detect air temperature in aquaponics, Raindrop sensors to detect rain, LDR sensors to detect clouds, Servo motors to move fish food. Gourami fish, grow lights instead of sunlight, 12c LCD to display information, water pump to circulate air from the aquarium or pond to the plants. The power consumption of this technology is around 216 watts per day when it is not raining, and around 375 watts per day when it is raining.

articleTitle: Interference Analysis Between LoRaWAN and the Wi-Fi HaLow (802.11ah)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: The development of Internet of Things (IoT) technology has advanced significantly, with technologies like LoRaWAN, Sigfox, ZigBee, and next-generation next-generation IoT (NB-IoT) being widely used. Wi-Fi HaLow, which offers better range and speed than LoRaWAN, is one such technology, but Indonesia lacks infrastructure to support it. This study analyzes the viability of Wi-Fi HaLow in Indonesia and its interaction with other IoT technologies, such as LoRaWAN, under interference conditions. Two scenarios are examined: interference from Wi-Fi HaLow to a LoRaWAN gateway and vice versa, using SEAMCAT software at 923 MHz. In this scenario, Wi-Fi HaLow serves as the interfering system, while LoRaWAN experiences disruption. The power variations of Wi-Fi HaLow were tested to identify the most efficient. Results show no interference at 8 km with 24 and 25 dBm, but interference occurs at 10 km with 26 dBm. Additionally, interference tests with varying numbers of Wi-Fi HaLow access points (APs) revealed minimal interference when the distance between the systems was 9 km, with interference rates ranging from 20% to 100%.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of H2S Gas Sensing: Pristine vs. Cobalt-Functionalized C2N Using First-Principles Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: The exceptional physical and electrical characteristics of two-dimensional Nitrogenated Holey Graphene (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>N) devices highlight their significance. C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>N-based sensors demonstrate remarkable sensitivity, stability, and responsiveness compared to other solid-state sensors. The conductivity of C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>N experiences shifts upon exposure to a wide array of organic and inorganic substances, enabling the detection of various target molecules through these conductivity alterations. Using first-principles transport simulations, a sensor device incorporating Nitrogenated Holey Graphene (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>N) is specifically designed to detect varying concentrations of hydrogen sulfide (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S) gas molecules. Through the utilization of the Quantumwise Atomistix Toolkit (ATK), a simulator for nanoscale semiconductor devices, a C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>N-based sensor is simulated in this study. This work studies the effectiveness of C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>N sensors, both pristine and functionalized with Co, for detecting varying concentrations of hydrogen sulfide (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S) gas molecules. Our findings reveal that the Co-functionalized C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>N sensor performs better than the pristine counterpart. Through simulations, we demonstrate the sensor's ability to detect single and double H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S molecules with 20% higher sensitivity and 15% improved selectivity compared to pristine C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>N. This research highlights the potential of C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>N-based sensors in gas sensing applications, including environmental monitoring and industrial safety, and notably in biomedical applications such as medical diagnostics through breath analysis for disease markers. The effectiveness of employing density functional theory for sensor analysis and electronic transport calculations is also highlighted.

articleTitle: Digital Artifact Analysis on Windows Subsystem for Android (WSA) based on ISO/IEC 27037:2012 and ISO/IEC 27042:2015
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: This study explores the characteristics of digital artifacts generated by the Windows Subsystem for Android (WSA) on the Windows 11 operating system. Utilizing ISO/IEC 27037:2012 and ISO/IEC 27042:2015 standards, the research encompasses the identification, collection, acquisition, preservation, analysis, interpretation, and reporting of digital artifacts found. The research methodology involves scenarios including the installation of WSA, usage of Android applications, and uninstallation of WSA to observe changes in the host system. The results indicate that the installation and usage of WSA produce various digital artifacts such as activity logs, application data files, and application usage metadata. The application of ISO/IEC digital forensic standards has proven effective in maintaining data integrity and authenticity during the investigation process. These findings can support similar digital forensic investigations in the future.

articleTitle: Solar Cell Efficiency under Varying Panel Angles and Temperature Conditions : An Experimental ANOVA Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: This study examines the impact of varying panel angles and temperatures on solar cell efficiency using Analysis of Variance (ANOVA). Conducted in Indonesia, the experiment explores panel inclination (90° to 70°) and ambient temperature (39°C to 43°C) effects on power output. Results indicate that at 90°, power output ranges between 54W to 60W, while at 70°, it drops to 45W to 49W. Additionally, higher temperatures lower the output, with power decreasing from 54W to 50W as the temperature rises from 39°C to 43°C. The ANOVA results show that slope has the greatest influence on efficiency with an Fo value of 111.4151, followed by temperature (Fo=31.38365). The interaction between these two factors, while present, had a smaller effect (Fo=1.132075). These results, compared against critical F-values, confirm the significance of both variables in optimizing solar cell performance.

articleTitle: Enhancing Code Smell Detection Performance in Python Programming Language : A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Code smell is one of the problems in programming which indicates that a problem has occurred, where there is something less than ideal in the code even though the code can run well. This research conducted a comparative study of the performance of Decision Tree, Random Forest, the use of the AdaBoost, CatBoost, XGBoost ensemble, and the use of SMOTEENN preprocessing to improve code smell detection in the Python programming language. Overall, the Decision Tree Pruning model hybrid with Adaboost and SMOTEEN produces the highest accuracy of 98.69% and MCC of 97.40%. Meanwhile, on the Long Method dataset, the XGBoost model with the SMOTEENN application produces the highest accuracy of 99.69% and MCC of 99.38%.

articleTitle: Comparing KNN and SVM for Aroma-Based Tuna Freshness Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Tuna is a vital commodity in Indonesia's fisheries industry, contributing significantly to the country's economy. Maintaining the quality of fishery products is essential, and one of the critical factors in ensuring this is the freshness of the fish, which determines its suitability for consumption and marketability. This research aims to develop an automated machine learning-based system capable of classifying the freshness of fish by analyzing the gases released during storage. Three gas sensors—MQ-135, MQ-9, and MQ-2—are employed to detect changes in the gas composition emitted by tuna and mackerel tuna. The data collected from the sensors is then processed using two classification methods, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) and Support Vector Machine (SVM), to determine the fish's freshness levels. The experimental results indicate that the machine learning models perform with remarkable accuracy. For tuna, both KNN and SVM achieve 99% accuracy. For mackerel tuna, KNN achieves an accuracy of 85%, while SVM performs with an accuracy of 99%. These findings highlight the system's potential for practical application in the fishing industry, ensuring consistent quality control of fishery products. The high accuracy rates, particularly for tuna, suggest that this system can contribute significantly to preserving fish quality and enhancing the value of Indonesia's fishery exports.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis of 'Kampus Merdeka' on Twitter Using Support Vector Machine (SVM) Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: This study aims to analyze public sentiment toward the Kampus Merdeka policy using Twitter data from January 2020 to February 2023. The policy, introduced by the Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology in Indonesia, allows students to gain real-world experience aligned with their interests as part of career preparation. Sentiment analysis used the keyword "Kampus Merdeka" to classify opinions as positive, negative, or neutral. The CRISP-DM (Cross Industry Standard Process for Data Mining) framework encompasses critical phases, including business understanding, data comprehension, data preparation, modeling, and evaluation. Sentiment labeling was performed using a lexicon-based approach, and the Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithm was applied for classification. The model's accuracy across different training and test data splits was 89.98%, 90.81%, and 91.18%, with the 90:10 split yielding the highest accuracy. Results showed that 57.17% of the tweets had positive sentiment, 26.77% were negative, and 16.10% were neutral. This study highlights the effectiveness of SVM in sentiment classification.

articleTitle: Automated Melanoma Detection Using Haar Wavelet-Based Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Melanoma is one of the most dangerous forms of skin cancer, with high potential for metastasis if not detected and treated early. Traditional diagnostic methods rely heavily on visual examination and dermoscopic analysis, which can be subjective and prone to errors. In this paper, we propose an automated melanoma detection system using Haar wavelet-based feature extraction combined with neural networks for classification. The Haar wavelet transform is employed to extract critical features from dermoscopic images, such as texture and edge details, which are crucial in distinguishing between benign and malignant lesions. These features are then used to train a MultiLayer Perceptron (MLP) neural network for accurate classification. Experimental results demonstrate that Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) algorithm achieves high accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, effectively reducing false positives and negatives. This system presents a reliable and efficient solution for early melanoma detection, which can assist dermatologists in clinical decision-making and potentially improve patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Security Patrolling System for Autonomous Navigation of Service Mobile Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Security and surveillance play a crucial role in maintaining the safety and integrity of the building surroundings. Conventional human security patrolling is subject to human error and limited by factors such as fatigue and inattentiveness. To tackle this challenge, a robot patrolling with 2D visual algorithm is proposed for collecting data from the IMU, LiDAR, and Raspberry Pi Camera to safely maneuver within the targeted environment. A hybrid waypoint and Rapidly-Exploring Random Tree (RRT) navigation algorithm is developed using the ROS platform. The Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) descriptor is integrated into the security patrolling robot to detect the presence of humans. Simulation and real-world testing have been conducted to evaluate the effectiveness and reliability of the developed system. As a result, the navigation system achieved 100% and 90% success rate in simulations and real-world environment tests respectively with the ability to detect humans with 95% accuracy in low visibility (nighttime) environments. The tree iteration value of 2000 was the best value to achieve the consistency of RRT navigation. The robot achieved maximum velocity of 0.26 m/s in obstacle free environment while the velocities to navigate with obstacles range between 0.1 m/s to 0.15 m/s.

articleTitle: PID Steering Control for Lane Keeping Assist based on IMU Sensor and ROS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: This study presents the development and implementation of a PID steering control system for lane-keeping assistance using an IMU sensor and ROS (Robot Operating System). The system leverages the capabilities of the Teensy 4.1 microcontroller and the HWT905-TTL IMU sensor to maintain precise steering adjustments, crucial for autonomous vehicle applications. The PID controller, designed to respond dynamically to real-time feedback, ensures that the motor reaches designated target angles, even under varying test conditions. The control system was tuned experimentally to achieve optimal response times, resulting in a rise time of approximately 2 seconds, a steady-state error within ±1-2 degrees, and a maximum overshoot of 4.09%. Performance metrics such as the Integral of Squared Error (ISE) and the Integral of Time-weighted Squared Error (ITSE) further confirmed system accuracy and stability over time. Results indicate that the proposed control system effectively maintains lane-keeping with minimal error, demonstrating potential for future deployment in real-world autonomous driving scenarios. Future work will focus on enhancing system adaptability through advanced tuning techniques and sensor fusion to improve robustness in dynamic environments.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Spatio-temporal Deep Learning for Hand Movement based on Motor Imagery Electroencephalography
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) in the Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) system is used to process signal data and translate it into a user context in this research case Motor Imagery (MI). MI data requires further learning, especially on features for EEG data classification. The evaluation method carried out and the comparison in this test is the use of spatio-temporal methods to analyze EEG signal patterns on each channel used and signal patterns that change over time. The EEG data used is SHU-Dataset which has data from 32 channels and data collection for 72 minutes on 25 subjects with each session is 5 sessions and 2 classes. The spatio-temporal methods used in SHU_Dataset testing, namely; SVM with CSP and FBCSP extraction features, FBCNet, DeepConvNet, EEGNet, EEGNex, and ATCNet. From the results on testing spatio-temporal methods, the best results are in the EEGNex and ATCNet methods with average accuracy results on EEGNex is 75.67% and on ATCNet 76.05%.

articleTitle: Optimizing Preacher Assignments Using AHC-PCA Algorithm in Kampar Regency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Inefficiencies in assigning preachers for Islamic preaching activities often arise due to distant placements, leading to delays and logistical challenges. In Kampar Regency, geographical diversity intensifies this issue, resulting in suboptimal preacher placements. This study aims to optimize preacher assignments by considering distance and mosque profiles. The dataset, which includes 102 mosques and 148 preachers was obtained from the Indonesian Ulema Council in Kampar. The Agglomerative Hierarchical Clustering (AHC) algorithm was selected for its capacity to cluster data across multiple characteristics. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was employed to reduce data dimensionality, thereby enhancing clustering outcomes. The optimization of the AHC-PCA algorithm generated an optimal clustering solution with a silhouette score of 0.625524 at three clusters. Furthermore, the elbow method also indicated that three clusters are optimal with a value of 390.234457, while the lowest Davies-Bouldin Index (DBI) score of 0.468573 was achieved with three clusters. Business Intelligence techniques visualized these clusters, providing a spatial distribution of preachers and mosques for detailed analysis. This study improves preacher assignments by reducing travel time and aligning preacher placements with mosque proximity and needs, thus enhancing the efficiency of Islamic preaching in Kampar Regency.

articleTitle: Coffee Defects Detection Based on Green Bean Images Using YOLO Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: The quality of coffee beans significantly impacts the overall value of coffee production, and detecting defective beans is a crucial step in ensuring high standards. The traditional coffee bean quality assessment process is time-consuming and subjective, relying heavily on the expertise of a Q grader. However, there is an alternative approach using deep learning technology to develop more portable and trainable tools that can achieve high accuracy. This study compares the performance of two deep learning-based object detection methods, YOLOv8 and YOLOv10, for detecting defects in green Arabica coffee beans, categorized into two different types of primary defects. The research methodology involved collecting data, preprocessing, designing models, training, and testing. The dataset consists of 700 images of coffee beans divided into two classes, brown beans and dried cherries. YOLOv8n achieved a test accuracy of mAP50 0.995 and mAP50-95 0.875, while YOLOv10n attained a test accuracy of mAP50 0.992 and mAP50-95 0.859. In terms of computational efficiency, YOLOv8n completed training in 0.499 hours, whereas YOLOv10n finished in 0.479 hours. Despite the marginal difference in accuracy, both models demonstrate high potential for real-time detection in the coffee industry, with YOLOv8n slightly outperforming YOLOv10n in accuracy, but YOLOv10n being slightly faster. These results suggest that both methods can be effectively utilized for defect detection, offering scalable solutions for the coffee processing industry, particularly in the sorting process, to ensure the production of high-quality, valuable coffee beans.

articleTitle: Dynamic Backlash Mitigation Using Adaptive PID for Precision Steering in Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Precision steering is crucial in autonomous vehicle control, where even minor inaccuracies can lead to significant navigation errors and compromised safety. This paper introduces a novel approach that integrates Adaptive Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) control with enhanced backlash compensation to improve steering accuracy in autonomous vehicles. The proposed method dynamically adjusts PID parameters in real-time based on the reference steering angle, ensuring optimal performance across various driving conditions. The backlash compensation mechanism effectively mitigates the nonlinearities caused by mechanical play in the steering system, a challenge that conventional PID controllers struggle to address. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed adaptive PID-enhanced backlash compensation method significantly reduces lateral tracking errors. The system achieved a maximum lateral deviation of only 0.01 meters at speeds of up to 25 m/s, with a mean square error of 1.752e-08, ensuring precise path-following performance. These results highlight the robustness and effectiveness of this approach for enhancing precision steering in autonomous vehicles.

articleTitle: VR Anima Safari Application with Design Thinking and Usability Testing Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: The rapid advancement of virtual reality (VR) technology has opened new possibilities for creating immersive and interactive experiences across various fields. This research addresses the challenge of enhancing visitor experiences at a large 13.9-hectare zoo in Surakarta, where exploring the entire area on foot can be tiring, especially in unfavorable weather. To solve this problem, the study developed Anima Safari, a VR application aimed at providing an engaging and educational exploration of wildlife in a simulated environment, thereby bridging the gap between entertainment and education. The application enables users to interact with diverse animal species and learn about their behaviors and habitats in an immersive way.The development process employed the Design Thinking methodology, which involved iterative prototyping and continuous refinement based on user feedback. Key stages included empathy-building, problem definition, ideation, prototyping, and testing. Usability testing was conducted using the Slovin formula to determine the sample size, involving 33 participants who provided quantitative feedback. The testing focused on four aspects: Learnability, Flexibility, Effectiveness, and Attitude.Results showed an overall usability score of 79.05%, indicating that Anima Safari is effective in delivering an educational and engaging experience. Strengths identified include the application's ability to provide a realistic and enjoyable safari experience, while areas for improvement were noted in navigation and system notifications. This study demonstrates the value of integrating Design Thinking and usability testing in VR application development, contributing to best practices for creating user-centered applications that meet educational and entertainment needs. Recommendations for future work include optimizing file size for better performance and expanding usability tests with larger user groups.

articleTitle: Optimizing Home Charging Infrastructure for Electric Vehicle Integration in Indonesian Power Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: This study highlights the challenges faced by PLN's electricity distribution network due to the rapid growth of electric vehicles (EVs) in Indonesia, with the number of EVs expected to increase from 67 thousand electric motorcycles in 2023 to 286 million by 2030. The objective of this research is to optimize the planning and integration of home charging infrastructure for EVs within the distribution network. The methodology includes qualitative and quantitative approaches, policy document analysis, and simulations to measure the impact of various levels of home charging penetration (0%-100%). Preliminary data indicate that the increased load from EV charging can cause issues such as power loss, voltage drop, and transformer overload, with home charging power requirements ranging from 2.2 kVA to 7.7 kVA, compared to the average load of 1.3 kVA for household-category customers. Preliminary conclusions suggest the need for comprehensive planning models and holistic solutions such as transformer additions and overnight charging policies to mitigate these negative impacts. The research hypothesis posits that proper infrastructure planning can support sustainable EV growth. The implications of this research provide practical guidance for the development of robust EV charging infrastructure and support the positive transformation towards electric mobility in Indonesia.

articleTitle: Coexistence Study of Low-Power Wide-Area Networks based on Wi-Fi HaLow (802.11ah) and Narrowband Internet of Things (NB-IoT)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: This study evaluates the possible coexistence between Wi-Fi HaLow (802.11ah) based Low-Power Wide-Area Networks (LPWAN) and non-no-technology (NB-IoT) systems. This study uses SEAMCAT software to analyze potential interference that may arise when both systems are operated simultaneously in the same environment. Both systems use the same frequency of 923 MHz, and the transmitting power used by Wi-Fi HaLow is 23, 24, and 25 dBm. The test results show that the interference probability of Wi-Fi HaLow to NB-IoT ranges from 20% to 100% when the number of active transmitters is varied from 1 to 5000. However, when varying the distance between the two systems, it was found that NB-IoT did not interfere with Wi-Fi HaLow when the distance was above 15 km, with 0% interference probability using 23 and 24 dBm power, while using 25 dBm power, mutual interference between Wi-Fi HaLow and NB-IoT still occurred up to a distance of 17 km, with 20% probability. The safe distance where no interference occurs is 18 km with 25 dBm power.

articleTitle: Clustering Preachers and Mosques for Effective Religious Outreach in Kampar Using DHC-PCA Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Preacher assignments to mosques in Kampar Regency have often been inefficient due to geographical distance and compatibility issues, limiting effective religious outreach. This study aims to optimize preacher assignments by applying the Divisive Hierarchical Clustering (DHC) algorithm. Analysis was conducted on a dataset of 250 records, clustering preachers and mosques based on geographical proximity and relevant attributes. Initial clustering modelling produced the highest silhouette score of 0.336. Dimensionality reduction using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) significantly improved the silhouette score to 0.8197, reflecting enhanced clustering quality. The elbow method validated eight clusters as optimal, with a value of 292.33. Research findings demonstrate that preachers can be effectively placed in geographically closer mosques aligned with their profiles, reducing inefficiencies. Business intelligence techniques visualized the clustering results, providing decision-makers with insights into geographical distribution and facilitating improved assignment strategies. These findings hold substantial implications for optimizing religious outreach in Kampar by minimizing logistical challenges and increasing engagement effectiveness.

articleTitle: Analyzing Cyberattack Patterns Using Cowrie Honeypot Deployed on a Raspberry Pi 5
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computer and Information Technology (ICEECIT)
abstract: Honeypots are essential tools in cybersecurity for monitoring, understanding, and mitigating cyber threats. This study examines attack patterns and commands executed by attackers within the Cowrie honeypot, which simulates interactive SSH and Telnet environments. Analyzing over 805,000 log entries collected over one month, this research identifies frequently used commands, session durations, and trends in attack frequency. Key findings reveal a strong preference for SSH over Telnet, with SSH commonly used in rapid, automated attacks, whereas Telnet sessions often involve longer, exploratory interactions. The study also highlights spikes in attack frequency, with over 100,000 attacks recorded on August 6, 2024. These insights enhance our understanding of attacker behavior and support improvements in intrusion detection and prevention systems.
